newsitem.title: GERMANY: Merck signs Chinese joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Merck signs Chinese joint venture.

text.p: German drugs group Merck KGaA has entered into a joint venture with a Chinese pharmaceutical group to produce and market Merck products in China, Merck said on Wednesday.

Merck said in a statement it had invested 50 million marks in the joint-venture with China National Pharmaceutical Industry Corporation (CNPIC) and that Merck would be a 90 percent partner, with CNPIC holding the other 10 percent.
The agreement establishing the joint venture, which will be called Merck Beijing Pharmaceuticals Ltd, was signed in Darmstadt and Merck said it hopes to take on 400 employees in coming years.
The market for pharmaceuticals in China is growing at 15 percent a year, twice as fast as in the West, Merck said.

Merck said that its high level of experience in research and development, marketing and distribution would combine with its partners' special local knowledge to make accessing the Chinese market easier.
Merck has had three stand-alone operations in China since 1994, in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou.
